exposure: Maternal Nutrient Excess (MNE) diet (45% energy fat and ad libitum fructose sodas)
outcome: Stress signaling (TLR4, TNFa, NF-kB p65, p38)
Expression of mitochondrial biogenesis regulators (PGC1a, PPARGC1B, PPARA, PPARB, CREB1, NOS3, SIRT1, SIRT3, NRF1)
Cytochrome C oxidase subunits I and II transcripts (cox1 and cox2)
cohort: Fetal baboons whose mothers were fed either a normal chow or a maternal nutrient excess diet before and during pregnancy.
finding: Maternal nutrient excess (MNE) in pregnant baboons induces stress signaling in fetal soleus muscle, leading to impaired mitochondrial biogenesis and lower mitochondrial content, which resembles changes seen in metabolic dysfunctions.
